findings.name: Contrastive Learning-Based Audio to Lyrics Alignment for Multiple Languages
findings.claim: Contrastive cross-modal embeddings reach <0.2 s average absolute error on Jamendo — alignment-tailored alternative to CTC transcription loss.
findings.design_implication: Contrastive lyrics alignment deepen.

findings.name: MFA Troubleshooting — singing atypical style
findings.claim: Official caveat: MFA is not intended to align single files that are long, noisy, or a different style such as singing — on-page only; further singing failure modes stay ·.
findings.design_implication: MFA singing caveat on-page; extras stay unverified.

findings.name: Source Level Debugging with LLVM
findings.claim: Analog: source AST objects map onto instruction ranges via debug metadata. Holds for discrete lyric/score tokens ↔ audio-frame spans under score-lock; limit: no continuous-time melisma or expressive lag.
findings.design_implication: Discrete lyric/score spans under score-lock.

findings.name: Towards Context-Aware Neural Performance-Score Synchronisation
findings.claim: Analog: Needleman–Wunsch Time Warping / DTW map performance ↔ score with warps and jumps. Holds for monotonic lyric↔timeline alignment; limit: classic NW/DTW assume structural agreement.
findings.design_implication: NW/DTW only under structural agreement.

findings.name: RFC 5905 NTPv4
findings.claim: Analog: two clocks share a reference; undisciplined skew accumulates. Holds for jam startSec vs Seed Audio [start:end] as dual timelines.
findings.design_implication: Dual clocks: jam startSec vs seed [start:end].

findings.name: Impact of Latency on Perceptual Judgments… in VR
findings.claim: Analog: HCI simultaneity / agency thresholds; delays above ~75 ms worsen felt sync. Holds for practice-companion UX of lyric lock; limit: perceptual threshold ≠ phoneme-boundary / MFA error.
findings.design_implication: ~75 ms UX threshold for lyric lock feel.

findings.name: When are initial consonants articulated in choral performance?
findings.claim: Analog: music pedagogy — initial consonants nearly always anticipated; vowel on the beat; lengthenability + surroundings matter. Holds strongly for lyric-to-note craft.
findings.design_implication: Vowel-on-beat; consonants anticipate.

findings.name: When Does a Sung Tone Start?
findings.claim: Sung tone onset is the vowel; accompanists lock piano attacks to vowel onset; consonant-to-beat lag about −100 to +300 ms.
findings.design_implication: Put the vowel nucleus on the MIDI beat; park onset consonants in the preceding gap.

findings.name: Montreal Forced Aligner user guide
findings.claim: Analog: speech forced alignment (Kaldi GMM/HMM orthography→phones). Does not transfer cleanly to singing — speech pipeline applied to sung duration variance.
findings.design_implication: Leave MFA speech→singing caveats unverified as transfer.

findings.name: Segment Duration and Proportion in Mandarin Singing
findings.claim: Speech C/V ratios would force 2.5-5 s consonants on a 10 s sung syllable; real singing dumps extra length onto the rime (onset max ~0.28 s).
findings.design_implication: Freeze onset/coda in a short band; leftover note length goes to the nucleus.

findings.name: Specifying Systems (TLA)
findings.claim: Analog: verification — Spec = Init ∧ □[Next]; stuttering steps are unobservable. Partial hold: expressive microtiming as stuttering around a score Spec; limit: discrete state machines, no continuous F0.
findings.design_implication: Partial: stuttering ≠ continuous F0 continuum.

findings.name: A Real-Time Lyrics Alignment System Using Chroma And Phonetic Features For Classical Vocal Performance
findings.claim: Live classical lyrics alignment combining chromagram with phonetic posteriorgrams under low-latency constraint.
findings.design_implication: Chroma+phonetic singing align.

findings.name: OpenUtau DiffSingerRhythmizerPhonemizer
findings.claim: Lyric→phonemes; ONNX rhythmizer inputs tokens/midi/midi_dur/is_slur → ph_dur; vowels stretched so note onsets align — note grid drives phone timing.
findings.design_implication: Score-grid phoneme×note in OpenUtau.

findings.name: NHSS
findings.claim: MFA word-boundary error is 25 ms on speech vs 104 ms on singing.
findings.design_implication: Do not trust speech MFA boundaries for PhonemeEvents.

findings.name: SongTrans
findings.claim: MFA labels melisma as silence, which then collides with true rests.
findings.design_implication: Slur/tie flags (or an explicit note-count head) are required.

findings.name: RMSSinger
findings.claim: Fine-grained SVS corpora force MFA then manual phoneme/note edits because one vowel may span multiple notes.
findings.design_implication: Prefer syllable/word→note maps (slurs for melisma) over phone-level forced alignment.

findings.name: Adapting pretrained speech model for Mandarin lyrics transcription and alignment
findings.claim: Whisper adapted to Mandarin singing yields lyrics alignment MAE 0.071 s on polyphonic pop.
findings.design_implication: Pretrained-speech transfer to sung lyric timing.

findings.name: OpenUtau DiffSingerVariance predict_dur
findings.claim: When predict_dur true, linguistic encode uses word_div/word_dur from vowel-grouped phones + note spans; else fixed ph_dur — dual path for predicted vs editor-fixed phone timing.
findings.design_implication: Predicted vs fixed phone timing paths.

findings.name: MakeDiffSinger README — MFA for acoustic training
findings.claim: Dataset pipeline names acoustic-forced-alignment make dataset from scratch with MFA for acoustic model training — MFA upstream labeling, not runtime score-lock.
findings.design_implication: MFA as DiffSinger dataset labeling only.

findings.name: RMSSinger: Realistic-Music-Score based Singing Voice Synthesis
findings.claim: Fine-grained SVS pipelines run MFA then manual phoneme/note edits because one vowel may span multiple notes; switches to word-level modeling.
findings.design_implication: MFA+manual; word-level vs phoneme-duration hard align.
findings.authors: He, Liu, Ye, Huang, Cui, Liu et al.

findings.name: Exploring Neural Transducers for End-to-End Speech Recognition (CTC vs attention)
findings.claim: CTC = hard monotonic latent alignments; attention = soft weighted frames. Holds for why CTC lyrics-to-audio ≠ lyrics-to-MIDI score-lock. Author per Verifier: Battenberg et al. (not Battenberg).
findings.design_implication: CTC vs attention analog hold-with-limit.

findings.name: ByteDanceSeedAudio
findings.claim: ByteDance Seed Audio [start:end] stamps are an absolute output timeline and write leading silence.
findings.design_implication: jam-sessions startSec/durationSec emit those stamps; Python is the clock.

findings.name: ACE-Step
findings.claim: ACE-Step duration/BPM sizes a latent canvas; it is not note MIDI.
findings.design_implication: ACE-Step cannot honor New Britain onsets.

findings.name: Sinsy
findings.claim: Sinsy time-lag: vowel onset tracks the score; consonants anticipate.
findings.design_implication: stamps should target vowel windows, not letter onsets.

findings.name: Hybrid CTC/attention ASR
findings.claim: CTC constrains monotonicity; attention alone is too flexible for speech order — prefer hard note/lyric schedules over free soft attention for practice lock.
findings.design_implication: Hybrid CTC constraint hold-with-limit.

findings.name: music21 lyricTimingsFromEvents / MIDI translate
findings.claim: Music IR keeps lyric meta timestamps separate from Note pitch/time — dual IR clocks; one Lyric tick does not encode melisma across many MIDI notes.
findings.design_implication: Lyric IR ≠ note IR hold-with-limit.

findings.name: pretty_midi Lyric container
findings.claim: pretty_midi Lyric events are separate from Note objects — dual-clock analog for lyric vs note schedules.
findings.design_implication: pretty_midi lyric container hold-with-limit.
